None of the 100 batch slots or 15 reserves is filled, so coverage, batch ordering and individual picks can't be reviewed and the selection step must run again. The findings below apply to the leftover pool (about 150 entries) that the re-run will choose from.

Pool facts are reliable. Every repo critical/high count I checked (about 60 entries) matched exactly, and star counts were within normal drift. Scan cost out of proportion to yield: microsoft/vscode has 220 MB of TS, and its 49 highs are mostly workspace-trust or policy bypasses that taint analysis can't find. Also opencode (40.8 MB TS, 3 critical/high), cline (31.4 MB, 2), super-productivity (34.9 MB, 1) and AFFiNE (24.9 MB, 1). Keep openclaw (436 MB TS, twice VS Code) for its 263 critical/high, but scan only its gateway packages and put it in the last batch. n8n (151 MB TS) and next.js (39.8 MB JS + 28.5 MB TS + 12.6 MB Rust) need the same package-level scoping.

Replay problems: 23 of Dokploy's 51 critical/high have no patched version, commit link or version mention. 20 of heyform's 21 critical/high have no patched_versions. All of adonisjs/core's advisories (1 critical, 3 high) are fixed in adonisjs/bodyparser (35 stars, no advisories of its own). requarks/wiki's advisories target v2 while the default branch is v3. hedgedoc's target 1.x on master while the default branch is develop (2.x). Resolve fix commits for each repo before giving it a slot.

Some advisories are not about the repo's own code: bruno's 2 criticals are npm supply-chain incidents, RSSHub's critical is a CI workflow, one cal.diy critical is a Next.js/React dependency CVE, and code-server's 2026 high is in the bundled Node.js Brotli decoder. Recall denominator: many pool advisories are authorization, IDOR or business-logic flaws (openclaw, n8n, OneUptime, novu, trigger.dev, better-auth, actualbudget) that source-to-sink analysis can't detect. Tag advisories by CWE and leave authz/logic CWEs (284/285/287/639/862/863) out of the recall denominator.

Libraries without entry points: axios, jsPDF, node-tar, protobuf.js, handlebars, sequelize, mongoose, simple-git, systeminformation, multer and socket.io would fill a whole batch with library-mode work. ToolJet's GitHub language is HTML (51 MB), with only 1 critical/1 high in a 1.77 GB repo. hedgedoc: 7,503 stars, TS, 1 critical/7 high (PDF-export file read, arbitrary upload, stored XSS) over Express, socket.io and DOM. All 8 list patched 1.x versions, so replay works from master and 1.x tags.

LoopBack has 0 advisories, a 469 MB repo and no popular apps. keystone: 9,986 stars, TS, 2 critical/2 high (field access-control bypass, reflected XSS, maxTake bypass), about 74k LOC. Adds GraphQL ground truth.

cube is mostly Rust (15.4 MB vs 8.9 MB TS), with 6 highs. storybook: 91,416 stars, 1 critical/3 high from 2025-26 (dev-server code injection, WebSocket hijacking). Fills the dev-server and socket gap; scan only the core dev-server package.

All 12 of multer's highs are DoS, with no source-to-sink path. mermaid: 90,946 stars, TS, 2 critical/2 high DOM XSS in diagram label rendering. Gives client-side sink ground truth for DOM and library mode.

Restify has 0 advisories and no popular apps. koa: 35,684 stars, 226 KB of JS, 1 critical/1 high (ReDoS, Host header injection via ctx.hostname). A small framework that the pool's Koa apps (strapi, budibase, outline, logto, nocobase) are built on.

code-server is a 0.3 MB TS wrapper around VS Code, and its 2026 high is a bundled Node.js Brotli decoder CVE, not its own code. serverless: 46,926 stars, JS, 1 high command injection in its MCP server's list-projects tool (fixed in 4.29.3). Adds a CLI/MCP tool-to-exec path.

VS Code is 220 MB of TS, and its 49 highs are mostly workspace-trust or agent-policy bypasses that taint analysis can't find. electerm (pool): 15.5k stars, 7 critical/15 high, Electron plus express-ws, a cheap IPC and socket replay.

opencode has 40.8 MB of TS for 1 critical/2 high. MCP inspector (pool) has 3 critical/4 high on the same pattern, a local server that leads to command execution (unauthenticated RCE, DNS rebinding), in 15.4 MB.
cline has 31.4 MB of JS/TS for 1 critical/1 high. dbgate (pool): Electron plus an Express API, 3 critical/4 high in 5.3 MB.
AFFiNE has 24.9 MB of JS/TS for 1 high. docmost (pool): NestJS on Fastify with Yjs websockets, 8 high (ZipSlip, path traversal, stored XSS) in 5.3 MB.

super-productivity has 34.9 MB of JS/TS for 1 high. tabby (pool): Electron and Angular, 1 critical/8 high (URL-handler RCE, drag-and-drop command injection) in about 1 MB of TS. Better Electron IPC ground truth.

method: Three discovery angles (npm advisory DB, self-hosted Node apps, framework/entry-point coverage); repo-level published critical/high advisory counts via gh api; critic spot-checked ~60 entries.
